passage: At the school canteen Arnab patted his empty pocket. "Lend me twenty, Gopika. We're best friends, aren't we?" It was the fifth time this month, and nothing from the earlier times had come back. Gopika's fingers curled around her coins. Her throat felt dry. What if he stopped sitting with her? "Not today," she said, very quietly. Arnab rolled his eyes. "Some best friend." Gopika ate her sandwich with hot cheeks, feeling both mean and used. That evening she told Mummy about it, and Mummy listened without interrupting and said they would think about it together.

qa.q: How many times had Arnab asked to borrow money this month?
qa.a: It was the fifth time this month.

qa.q: What was Gopika afraid of when Arnab asked again?
qa.a: She was afraid he would stop sitting with her if she said no, even though she felt used and mean at the same time.

qa.q: What could Gopika do if Arnab keeps asking?
qa.a: Politely refuse again and keep talking with a parent about it, as she began to do with Mummy.

qa.q: How might Arnab see the moment when Gopika said no?
qa.a: He may have been annoyed at hearing a no from someone who usually said yes; his "Some best friend" suggests he hoped friendship would make her agree.

grounding: Illustrates a child pressed by a friend who keeps borrowing money on the strength of friendship, feeling used but afraid to say so.
